Subject: Post-call: Model fit & quantization tradeoffs (FinTechCo)

Hi Oliver / Priya —

Great to speak earlier — thanks for the context on the risk-notification use case and the 1.5-2.5k token average sequence lengths you typically see. Quick recap + next steps from our side: 

Summary from call
- Primary goals: high throughput for nightly scoring pipeline, 95th percentile latency target ~150ms for inference path, and strict PII handling with audit logs.
- Current blocker: model quality/cost trade-off and team experience with quantized weights.

What I’m sending you today
- Model-fit evals we ran on a representative prompt set (attached: fintech-prompt-sets.csv).
- A short model evaluation report (attached PDF) that includes accuracy/QA-style pass rates on your prompt set and latency/throughput measured on our Dedicated profile.
- Benchmarks link: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/ftc-crypto-2026 - contains token-level latency graphs and per-model cost estimates.

High-level recommendations (based on the eval):
1) Candidate models to prioritize for a pilot:
   - Llama-2-13B-chat (quantized AWQ / GPTQ profiles) - best balance of quality and cost for your prompt set.
   - Mistral-Instruct-7B - lower cost, slightly lower pass-rate on complex reconciliation prompts. Good for lower-latency paths.
   - Falcon-40B-instruct (if you want higher headroom for edge cases) - higher infra cost but stronger on long context reasoning.

2) Quantization tradeoffs we observed (summary):
   - AWQ 4-bit: typically 1-3% drop in end-task pass-rates vs fp16 baseline, throughput improvements ~1.8-2.4x depending on sequence length.
   - GPTQ 4-bit: slightly higher variance; 2-4% pass-rate drop but can be tuned per-layer, throughput ~2.0x on our Dedicated profile.
   - FP8 (hardware dependent): near fp16 quality on many prompts, with 2.5-3x throughput on supported accelerators - requires hardware that supports FP8 kernels.

Recommended next steps
- Technical deep-dive with Rishi (SE) and Vivek (solutions) to look at your exact token distribution and run a short canary on 1-2 models (we can run the AWQ and GPTQ profiles side-by-side).
- Quick POC timeline: 2 weeks to run thorough per-model/quantization evals, then a 1-week canary in staging.

I’ve attached the evaluation PDF and the prompt set we used. Rishi/Vivek - can you please prepare a short trade-study slide (2-3 slides) summarizing latency, throughput, and expected quality delta across AWQ/GPTQ/FP8 for FinTechCo’s distribution?

Oliver / Priya - open to scheduling the technical deep-dive this week or early next. What times work for you?

Thanks,

Marissa Cole

Quick trade-study summary (2-3 bullets each) - happy to present.

Hardware/FP8 validation
- FP8 validated on NVIDIA H100 (cloud and on-prem variants) and Aurora X instances that expose FP8 kernels. Caveat: older A100-like fleets typically do not have FP8 kernel support; FP8 requires both runtime and driver stack compatibility.

Throughput / quality deltas (measured on Redwood Dedicated profile, mixed-batch workload approximating FinTechCo distribution):
- AWQ (4-bit): throughput +1.8-2.2x vs fp16 at 512 tokens; +2.0-2.4x at 2k tokens. Typical pass-rate delta: -1.0% to -3.0% on our prompt sets (worst on multi-step reconciliation prompts).
- GPTQ (4-bit): throughput +2.0x across lengths; pass-rate delta: -2.0% to -4.0% with higher variance across seeds - good for cost-sensitive pilots where per-layer tuning is possible.
- FP8: throughput +2.5-3.0x on supported hardware; pass-rate delta: ~0% to -1% (closest to fp16).

Notes on short vs long sequences
- Short (<512 tokens): quantization overheads are relatively higher (less KV cache amortization) so measured throughput gains are slightly muted vs long sequences. Expect AWQ gains closer to 1.6-1.9x on short contexts.
- Long (~2k tokens): caching and compute amortization improves relative throughput; AWQ and FP8 show better scaling.

Canary & monitoring recommendations
- Canary size: start with 0.5-1% of nightly scoring traffic (non-customer-facing). If no regressions at 48 hours, ramp to 5% for one week, then to 10% with continuous monitoring.
- Monitoring checklist: per-prompt pass-rate, token-level probability shifts, latency p50/p95/p99, error spikes, and end-to-end cost delta. Add automated regression alerts if pass-rate drops by >2% or token-prob KL divergence exceeds threshold.

Deliverables we can push before the deep-dive
- 2-slide summary with the numbers above + suggested canary plan.
- A reproducible eval job we can run against FinTechCo’s private prompt set (requires a short S3/Drive share).

Oliver - are you able to share a private link to a secure S3/Drive with a small sample (500 prompts) for us to run against your real distribution? If yes, we’ll run the AWQ/GPTQ/FP8 sweep and share a side-by-side report.
